attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known nonrelativizing locality-extraction theorem converts an arbitrary small H_N circuit into local SAT-range separators with only N^{o(1)} loss.
steps: Fix d>1 and q,rho<1+epsilon; the substitution equation still gives the desired target consequence from a true C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} lower bound.

assumptions: epsilon>0 is fixed and all o(1) terms are uniform over fixed SAT exponent c.
The target bridge is nonuniform P/poly but the generator is uniform or has explicitly charged nonuniformity N^rho.
A relativizing extractor may inspect H_N, G_N, and oracle SAT labels, but not syntactic facts special to the real Cook-Levin SAT relation.
Separator covers are charged by D N^sigma log N plus EN, including greedy-cover overhead and exact correction.
definitions: source object: the Boolean carrier H_N(x)=OR_{j<=N^q} SAT(G_N(x,j)) on N-bit x, with generator size N^rho and query length L=(log N)^d.
target object: the route-level consequence SAT notin P/poly obtained from C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} plus the substitution bridge, not the full P != NP conjecture.
controlled interface: substitute a size L^c SAT circuit into each generated query; the only target cost is N^rho+N^q L^{O(c)}.
target-preserving condition: d>1, (1+epsilon)/2<q<1+epsilon, rho<1+epsilon, uniform G_N, and no advice or oracle bit outside the generated SAT instances.
one-sided separator cover: local predicates of size N^sigma that hit at least one positive generated bag and reject every negative bag, with E exceptional bags patchable by equality circuits.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Need a SAT-specific influence lower bound under an honest encoding for the AC0 consequence; no gap remains for SIZE transfer because parity is the decisive falsifier.
steps: Fix the total SAT_m encoding and define I on the same m coordinates; a lower bound L_m excludes exactly target classes with B_T(m)<L_m.
For AC0_d[m^k], use the Boppana average-sensitivity bound B_T=O_d((k log m)^{d-1}); a super-polylog influence lower bound would be a valid restricted lower bound.
Try T=SIZE(m^k). PARITY_m lies in SIZE(O(m)) subset SIZE(m^k) for k>=1 and has I=m, while every Boolean function has I<=m.
Thus any influence threshold rejecting all SIZE(m^k) circuits must exceed m, impossible; the route is quarantined for P-vs-NP transfer.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The result is a conditional restricted-class bridge and a route failure certificate, not evidence for the main P != NP conjecture.

assumptions: SAT_m is totalized by rejecting malformed encodings; all influence is measured over the resulting m input bits.
Truth-table constructivity for the audit costs poly(N) with N=2^m; this makes high-influence predicates natural when their density is polynomial.
The lemma is a target gate, not a claim that the needed SAT influence lower bound is known.
definitions: source object: Boolean slice f_m=SAT_m:{0,1}^m->{0,1} under a fixed honest total encoding; route claims a lower bound on total influence I(f_m).
target object: T_{d,k}=AC0 depth d size m^k, or T_k=SIZE(m^k) for the rejected extrapolation.
controlled interface: every target circuit C in T must satisfy an a priori influence ceiling B_T(m,k,d), with no change of input encoding or padding.
target-preserving condition: prove I(SAT_m)>B_T on the same m-bit slice; padding, promise restriction, and advice bits must not hide measured coordinates.
AC0 ceiling uses De Morgan basis, unbounded fan-in, fixed depth d, and size s=m^k.
For unrestricted circuits, parity is small and maximally influential, so any threshold using only I(f) is not useful.

falsifiers: PARITY_m is a falsifier for SIZE transfer: linear-size circuits attain I=m, so high influence cannot be useful against polynomial size.
Padding falsifier: H(x,z)=SAT_m(x) on M=m+m^beta bits preserves raw core influence but changes normalized influence and size thresholds.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known construction supplies an E-uniform low-D selector whose rows are robustly outside all subthreshold correction balls while its indexed bit relation lacks subthreshold circuits. Standard pseudorandomness repairs are too locally explicit; sequential-only repairs still need an E bit algorithm for the aggregate target.
steps: Start from the valid random calibration: 2^{D m} independent rows almost surely avoid every sparse-correction ball around circuits of size 2^{epsilon m}/4.
Try to replace the random rows by a seed-efficient generator G_m:{0,1}^{D m}->{0,1}^{2^m} using k-wise independence, an NW design, or a locally computable code; define T_{m,j}=G_m(j).
Observe that every standard derandomized generator exposes a bit decoder B_m(j,x)=G_m(j)_x of size poly(m) or at worst 2^{gamma m} with gamma<epsilon.
Hardwire j into B_m. This gives circuits for every selected row below 2^{epsilon m}, contradicting the intended MCSP no-side claim before extraction starts.

To avoid the contradiction, demand decoder circuit exponent at least epsilon-o(1). But then proving the generator has a hard row proves the aggregate decoder lower bound, which is exactly the target-preserving E lower bound after padding.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The audit proves a valid falsifier for a large class of selector repairs, not a new lower bound. It does not construct the required non-natural, no-advice, decoder-hard low-D carrier.

assumptions: D, epsilon, gamma, and kappa are fixed positive constants with epsilon<1.
MCSP size is measured by unrestricted Boolean circuits over m input bits.
The row index j may be hardwired when upper-bounding the circuit complexity of a single row.
The decoder family is nonuniform for the upper-bound falsifier; uniformity only strengthens the invalidation.
definitions: source object: an E-uniform low-image family of truth tables T_{m,j}:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, with j in [M_m] and M_m<=2^{D m}.
target object: the padded aggregate E language A(j,x,pad)=T_{m,j}(x) on length n=kappa(1+D)m+O(1).
controlled interface: a bit decoder B_m taking row index j and input x, plus a streaming verifier only if it does not give subthreshold random access.
target-preserving condition: the same unrestricted circuit model, no advice in length selection, fixed constants D, epsilon, kappa, and padding that preserves the exponent conversion.

equations.label: image_and_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when image entropy D and MCSP threshold epsilon are fixed constants independent of m.

equations.label: decoder_to_row_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when B_m computes every requested table bit and the row index j may be hardwired as nonuniform constants.

equations.label: succinct_decoder_collapse
equations.valid_when: Applies when the decoder upper bound is measured in the same unrestricted circuit model as the MCSP threshold.

equations.label: padded_decoder_ceiling

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed low-D carrier offers bit access by circuits below 2^{epsilon m-o(m)}, reject the source even if its combinatorial avoidance proof is valid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-specific bridge repair and falsifier: it gives the exact explicitness threshold a selector must beat before it can support MCSP carrier extraction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Succinct bit-decoder collapse for explicit selector repairs: let I_m={T_{m,j}:j<M_m} be a low-image MCSP carrier with M_m<=2^{D m} and threshold s_m=2^{epsilon m}. If a bit decoder B_m(j,x)=T_{m,j}(x) has unrestricted circuits of size 2^{gamma m+o(m)} with gamma<epsilon, then every decoded row is below the intended MCSP no-side threshold. Hence standard PRG, k-wise, NW, local-code, or lexicographically unranked selectors with succinct random access are a falsifier for this source route, not a valid source theorem.

assumptions: Circuit encoding overhead is O(s log s+s log m).
Sparse correction of r positions costs O(rm) gates by equality tests and OR-composition.
definitions: bad ball: all truth tables within Hamming distance r of a subthreshold circuit truth table.
robust row hardness: distance greater than r from every circuit of size at most s/4, which blocks sparse corrections of size O(rm).
low-D random image: a multiset of at most 2^{D m} independently sampled truth tables.

equations.label: bad_ball_volume
equations.valid_when: Valid when bad tables are defined as radius-r corrections of unrestricted circuits of size at most s over m inputs.

equations.label: calibrated_measure
equations.latex: r=\lfloor s/(c m)\rfloor,\ s=2^{\epsilon m}\ \Longrightarrow\ \mu_{\mathrm{bad}}\le 2^{-2^m+O(2^{\epsilon m}m^2)}.
equations.valid_when: Applies in the sublinear threshold regime epsilon less than one with polynomial circuit-description overheads.

equations.label: low_image_random_success
equations.valid_when: Requires only exponentially many in m sampled rows and independent uniform truth tables.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If epsilon reaches one, D grows like 2^m, or the correction radius is macroscopic, this counting certificate no longer supports the route.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantitative calibration showing the route fails at E-uniform non-natural selection, not at the bad-ball counting bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Random low-D robust carriers exist with overwhelming probability, so the current obstruction is explicitness, not combinatorics. For N=2^m, s=2^{epsilon m}, and correction radius r=floor(s/(c m)), the union of all radius-r balls around circuits of size at most s/4 has measure 2^{-N+O(2^{epsilon m}m^2)}. Thus 2^{D m} independent random rows avoid the bad set with probability 1-o(1).

assumptions: The aggregate language is E-computable within the declared padding budget.
The lower bound target is nonuniform unrestricted circuit size, not only uniform algorithms or restricted gates.
definitions: aggregate bit relation: B_m(j,x)=T_{m,j}(x) with |j|<=Dm and |x|=m.
row-to-aggregate transfer: hardwiring j in any circuit for B_m gives a circuit for row T_{m,j}.
circularity warning: a selector whose correctness proof assumes B_m is hard has assumed the extracted lower bound.

equations.label: aggregate_row_equivalence
equations.valid_when: Valid when B_m is the complete indexed truth-table decoder and circuits may hardwire a fixed row index.

equations.label: aggregate_extraction_exponent
equations.valid_when: Applies after the aggregate language includes the row index, preserves uniform padding, and has no nonuniform length selector.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A proposed derandomized selector is invalid if its bit relation is intentionally easy; it is circular if its proof first establishes the same aggregate lower bound needed as output.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Circularity audit: it separates genuine source construction from merely hiding the desired lower bound inside the decoder.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Bit-relation dichotomy for low-image carriers: for any E-uniform aggregate bit relation B_m(j,x), existence of a row with MCSP complexity above 2^{epsilon m} is equivalent, up to O(Dm) hardwiring, to an aggregate lower bound for B_m at exponent epsilon/(1+D). Therefore an easy decoder refutes the source, while proving the decoder hard is already the target-preserving consequence of the route.

control_decision.pivot_test: If every plausible E-uniform carrier necessarily supplies a bit decoder of exponent gamma<epsilon, certify route failure by nonuniform leakage and threshold collapse.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only upon a no-advice low-D carrier with an E-computable aggregate bit relation and a non-natural proof of a row lower bound above 2^{epsilon m}, preserving delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
control_decision.reason: The bridge theorem is still valid, but the source construction space is narrower: explicit selector proofs must certify absence of subthreshold indexed decoding, not merely avoidance by counting.

dependency_updates.description: The valid transfer from an actual hard row to an aggregate E lower bound remains delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
Explicitness cannot mean locally easy bit access; the bit relation must avoid circuits below 2^{epsilon m-o(m)} or the source collapses.
Standard PRG, k-wise, NW, and local-code selectors fail by decoder leakage unless their bit relation is already hard.

falsifiers: Any k-wise independent, NW, algebraic-code, or PRG selector with bit decoder size 2^{gamma m} for gamma<epsilon is a source falsifier.
A lex-first table outside the bad-ball union is not valid unless its bit predicate is E-computable without enumerating 2^{Theta(2^{epsilon m})} circuits.
A dense E-decidable property excluding small circuits would be a natural-proofs barrier interaction, not an acceptable non-large carrier certificate.
Nonuniform advice choosing a good row destroys the target-preserving condition and yields only a nonuniform leakage statement.
If D or kappa makes epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) vanish, the extraction threshold collapses even from a valid hard row.
Aggregate evidence in a restricted or uniform circuit model does not certify MCSP no-side hardness against unrestricted circuits.
